items.ruling: The long hall and the flooded hall stay WINDOWLESS; bible/color_script.json is the side that moves. SCN-long-hall keeps 'no windows, no skylights' and 25 blind halo roundels, and its lighting.json keeps roundel_glow = reflected_lamplight_only. color_script's scene_curves and the act-level stained_glass doses (ep01 acts 3-6, ep02 act 1, ep05 act 3) now carry the identical pastel dose as SURFACE colour - jewel glints and lead-came sheen on the blind roundels where a lamp hangs close, the pastel tulip lamp shades, the mosaic dado and floor border - with no pool of coloured light anywhere, and the garden green through the little door left as the hall's only coloured cast light (SPC-long-hall-01). SCN-pool-of-tears has no shaft: the way-out light Alice swims toward is the field of lamp reflections at the south end, where the reflections crowd and the shore steps lie - the heading that scene's own lighting.json dream_growth already named, now recorded there as way_out_heading. SCN-courtroom is untouched: it has real high stained-glass windows per its architecture.json, so it keeps its cast stained-glass light and style.json CR-007 ('daylight through stained glass MAY cast soft pastel colour... that is the only coloured light') stays satisfied.
ruling_basis: 1. Source text beats inferred design (WRITE_RULES.md section 1): ch001-p11 'lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof' and ch001-p14 'that dark hall' anchor architecture.json; the roundel-WINDOW reading was inferred with no source anchor and would add an unwritten light source to a hall the source calls dark.

2. The later, narrower ruling on the same fact wins: roundel_glow was decided on 2026-09-23 by p4-cr-architecture / p4-cr-lighting-2 under BIB-0027, closing DEF-p4-cr-architecture-001-b. color_script's BIB-0027 amendment was written in the same parallel batch and never re-read against those amended openings, so it is the stale side of the disagreement, not a live second opinion.
3. Two scene files against one plan file for the pool: SCN-pool-of-tears inherits SCN-long-hall and already carried key_source oil_lamp_row, daylight_access lamplit_no_sky and no shaft.

4. Irreversibility: a window opening is architecture, not decoration. The whiteboxes and layout packs for both scenes are H2-locked at G4 (runs/g4/gate.json), ep01's storyboard is delivered against the windowless reading, and the re-roll budget is 0.

5. Design: the little-door garden green is the film's designed way-out colour and the one motivated bright thing ep01 act 3 is built around. A second daylight source in the hall would compete with it; a daylight shaft in the pool would duplicate its job.

items.ruling: It IS a collision: change_id is ONE GLOBAL namespace, not a per-file one - WRITE_RULES.md section 5 step 2 requires a duplicate check before writing, and every citation in bible/ and qa/ is a bare 'BIB-NNNN' with no file qualifier, so a per-file scope would make those citations unresolvable. The tie is broken by the register: bible/changelog.md is where an id is actually allocated. The entry already logged there (task p4-h2-bible, ~20 citations across costumes.json, characters/** and qa/defects/**) KEEPS BIB-0029; the creature.json amendment (task p4-h2-creature), which never reached the changelog, moves to BIB-0032 and receives the changelog entry it was missing (WRITE_RULES.md P-011).
items.uniqueness_check: BIB-0001..BIB-0031 were in use across bible/, qa/, runs/, directing/ and story/ before writing; BIB-0032 and BIB-0033 were free and are the only two ids added by this task.
items.signed_gate_check: No signed gate file was renumbered, because neither cites BIB-0029: runs/g4/gate.json cites only BIB-0027 (three mentions) and runs/g5-ep01/gate.json cites no BIB id at all.
items.citations_not_updated: runs/p4-h2-creature/result.json, runs/p4-h2-creature/meta.json and runs/dag.json still say BIB-0029. Run receipts are immutable records of what a task wrote at the time and were deliberately not rewritten; the redirect is the supersedes field on the BIB-0032 changelog entry - a BIB-0029 citation dated to task p4-h2-creature means BIB-0032.
items.rule_for_next_parallel_batch: Precedent P-013 (bible/WRITE_RULES.md section 7.4): BIB numbers are one global namespace and bible/changelog.md is the register, so agents DO NOT self-assign a literal number. Since every write already goes through memory-bible (WRITE_RULES.md section 1), the writing agent proposes "change_id": "BIB-PENDING" with its task_id and memory-bible stamps the real number at the moment it appends the changelog entry - one writer, one register, no race. An agent writing its own file under a defect (P-011) does the same. Writing a literal number without checking bible/changelog.md first is a section 5 step 2 failure.
